Class VisionCamera

java.lang.Object
yall.VisionCamera
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
Direct Known Subclasses:
LimelightWrapper, PhotonVisionWrapper, SynapseWrapper
public abstract class VisionCamera extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A camera from any supported vendor, with one API for targets and robot pose estimates. On a real robot it reads the vendor's library; in simulation it reads a PhotonVision camera simulation in a VisionSim world, so the same robot code runs in both.

Create one with the wrapper for the camera's vendor: 

VisionCamera front = new LimelightWrapper(new Limelight("limelight-front"), frontConfig);
VisionCamera back = new PhotonVisionWrapper(new PhotonCamera("back"), backConfig);
VisionCamera side = new SynapseWrapper(new SynapseCamera("side"), sideConfig);

Call update() once per loop (or VisionSystem.update() for several cameras), then read getLatestResult(), getEstimatedPose() and the other getters. They all report what the last update() read.

    • update

      public void update()
      Reads new frames from the camera (or its simulation), filters their pose estimates, counts the filter's decisions and publishes telemetry. Call once per loop, before the getters.

    • setRobotOrientation

      public void setRobotOrientation(Rotation3d orientation, AngularVelocity yawRate)
      Gives the camera the robot's orientation on the field. PoseEstimationMode.HEADING_ASSISTED needs it every loop, and the pose filter's yaw rate check uses the yaw rate.

      The yaw must be the robot's heading on the field, your pose estimator's rotation, not the gyro's own reading: resetting the pose estimator turns its heading without turning the gyro. The roll and pitch come from the gyro.

      Parameters:
      orientation - Robot orientation on the field (blue-origin, counterclockwise positive yaw).
      yawRate - Robot yaw rate.

    • setRobotToCamera

      public void setRobotToCamera(Distance forward, Distance left, Distance up, Angle roll, Angle pitch, Angle yaw)
      Moves the camera on the robot, for a camera on a turret or other moving mechanism. Takes the same measurements as VisionCameraConfig.withRobotToCamera(Distance, Distance, Distance, Angle, Angle, Angle).
      Parameters:
      forward - Distance forward of the robot center.
      left - Distance left of the robot center.
      up - Height above the floor.
      roll - Rotation about the camera's forward axis.
      pitch - Rotation about the left axis. Negative tilts the camera up.
      yaw - Rotation about the up axis, counterclockwise positive.

    • getCameraFieldPose

      public Optional<Pose3d> getCameraFieldPose()
      Where the camera itself is on the field, worked out from the AprilTags in the newest frame alone. It doesn't use the robot pose or the camera offset, so it can measure them: for example a turret's angle, with getCameraYawOnRobot(Rotation2d).

      Each AprilTag the camera solved gives a camera pose: the tag's place on the field, moved back along the camera-to-tag transform. The closest tag's is returned, because it is the most accurate.

      Returns:
      The camera's pose on the field, or empty if the newest frame has no solved AprilTag on the field.

    • getCameraYawOnRobot

      public Optional<Rotation2d> getCameraYawOnRobot(Rotation2d robotHeading)
      Which way the camera points relative to the robot, from what it sees: the camera's heading on the field (getCameraFieldPose()) minus the robot's heading. For a camera on a turret, this is the turret's angle (plus any angle the camera is mounted at on the turret), so it can check or zero the turret's encoder.
      Parameters:
      robotHeading - The robot's heading on the field, your pose estimator's rotation.
      Returns:
      The camera's yaw on the robot, counterclockwise positive, or empty if the newest frame has no solved AprilTag on the field.
